mappings.note: Why Indian mobile and data prices collapsed from 1990s levels. A market-and-policy question; goal-level CG-SST4, since this frame has no infrastructure outcome and C-SST4.2's LOs are a local market visit and a State office report. (Empty answer on this row; see report.)

Asking older relatives how long-distance messages travelled before mobiles. Cited at competency level: C-SST4.2 is the only place in this frame naming 'the public works undertaken in one's own locality', and no LO under it covers communications.

Social infrastructure - schools, hospitals, police stations, libraries - and how it supports a community. C-SST4.2 for local public provision, LO-138 because several of those are State government offices in one's own locality.
Making infrastructure sustainable, worked through an eco-friendly school. LO-123, conservation of energy and resources; LO-122 is rejected because no pollution source is analysed.
Listing five infrastructure problems observed locally and proposing fixes. C-SST4.2 for local public works, LO-131 for interpreting an issue in one's own region.
What happens to a Maharashtra tomato farmer if one piece of the infrastructure puzzle is missing. Competency-level C-SST4.2 for interlocking public works; no LO reaches infrastructure.
The stalls, vendors and shops that cluster around a railway or metro station. LO-137 is a genuine fit - observing how a local market works - rather than the infrastructure fallback.
A Community Responsibility Pact for looking after public infrastructure. C-SST4.2 for the public works, LO-131 for the civic issue in one's own locality.

Mapped on what the row actually answers - how a new highway changes life in a nearby village. Competency-level C-SST4.2 for public works and their local effect. (Stem is a corrupted run of textbook headings and an advertising line; see report.)
What the loss of internet and phone service would do to work and study. Competency-level C-SST4.2 for communications as public infrastructure.
What physical infrastructure has appeared locally in the last decade and what one would build. Competency-level C-SST4.2, which names public works in one's own locality.
How ports, highways and airports create direct and indirect employment. An economy-wide question, so goal-level CG-SST4 rather than the locality-scoped C-SST4.2.
Weighing environment against new roads and airports, and whether both can be had. LO-123 for conservation, LO-122 for the pollution the question asks students to weigh.
How roads, airports and communications help during floods or earthquakes. LO-121 is a direct fit - preventive and responsive action in the event of disaster. (Empty answer on this row; see report.)
Shanghai as the busiest container port by TEU. Global trade volume, so goal-level CG-SST4; CG-SST1 is not added because no locating is required.
Indian Railways as the country's largest employer at about 1.21 million. Employment and the economy, goal-level CG-SST4.
Track-side alarms in forest stretches to keep elephants from being struck. LO-123, sensitivity to conserving fauna; LO-121 is rejected because this is a designed safeguard, not a disaster.
Bhakra Nangal in Himachal Pradesh. A major public work; competency-level C-SST4.2, and CG-SST1 is not added because the state is recalled, not located.
Innovations in infrastructure that improve mobility, with electric vehicles as the worked example. C-SST4.2 for the public works, LO-123 because the case for them is cleaner energy.
Physical infrastructure defined as the tangible network of roads, pipelines and cables. Competency-level C-SST4.2 for public works; no LO in this frame reaches the concept.
Indian Railways as the fourth-largest system in the world. Public works at national scale, competency-level C-SST4.2.
The Arthashastra prescribing 16 metres for royal highways. An ancient text read for its content; goal-level CG-SST2, since CG-SST2's competencies stop at kingdoms, monuments and religion.
E-governance as government delivering services online, with DigiLocker as the example. LO-138, the functioning of a government office as a citizen meets it.
A patent as the exclusive right to make, use or sell an invention. An economic and legal institution; goal-level CG-SST4, no LO covering it.
Assertion-reason on vandalism of public infrastructure as everyone's loss and everyone's bill. C-SST4.2 for the public works, LO-131 for the civic issue in one's own locality.
India's 159 airports as of 2025. Public works at national scale, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Railways aiming for 100 percent electric traction. LO-122 for the pollution being cut, LO-123 for the energy-conservation goal behind it.
All India Radio beginning broadcasts in 1930. LO-136, the role of media; the other communications-technology items carry C-SST4.2 because they are about the network rather than about mass media.

Metro benefits - speed, less congestion, cleaner air - against the false claim that metros haul bulk cargo. C-SST4.2 for the public work, LO-122 for the air-pollution benefit that is one of the scored options.
Shipping as the cheapest way to move coal, cars and cement over long distances. Transport infrastructure, competency-level C-SST4.2.
The fibre, towers, satellites and data centres a voice note travels through. Communications infrastructure, competency-level C-SST4.2.

Observing misuse of public space - graffiti, broken streetlights, damaged benches - its cost and its remedies. C-SST4.2 for the public works, LO-131 for reading a local civic issue. (Answer is a heading with no body; see report.)
India's road network second only to the United States. Public works at national scale, competency-level C-SST4.2.
The Arthashastra's penalties for breaking a reservoir dam or a park hedge. An ancient text on protecting public works; goal-level CG-SST2, matching the road-width item.

Alexander Bain's fax machine of 1843 on the communications timeline. Competency-level C-SST4.2 for the communications strand of infrastructure; LO-136 is reserved for items about mass media's public role.

J.C. Bose's coherer as a receiver in early wireless. Communications technology, competency-level C-SST4.2; CG-SST2 is rejected because the chapter treats it as infrastructure history, not as a historical source.
Nearly 900 million internet connections in India by 2025. Digital infrastructure at national scale, competency-level C-SST4.2.
A flood-prone coastal city choosing elevated flood-proof highways and reinforced bridges. LO-121 for preventive action against a recurring disaster, C-SST4.2 for the public works chosen.

Mapped on what the row answers - the Arthashastra's 2.5-metre chariot road against the 16-metre royal highway. Goal-level CG-SST2 for the ancient text. (Stem asks about J.C. Bose but the options and key belong to the Arthashastra question; see report.)

Assertion-reason rejecting philanthropy as the motive for British railways, against extraction of cotton and rapid troop movement. C-SST4.2 for the railway as a public work, CG-SST2 for the colonial purpose behind it.
NH44 from Srinagar to Kanyakumari as the longest national highway. Public works, competency-level C-SST4.2.

Buses designed with ramps and low floors for elderly and disabled passengers. C-SST4.2 for the public provision, LO-131 because accessible design is an equality question about who a public service actually serves.

The Dhola Sadiya Bridge over the Lohit keeping Assam and Arunachal connected when ferries fail in flood. Competency-level C-SST4.2 for the public work; LO-121 is not added because the bridge is identified, not the flood response.
Railways introduced in 1853 to move cotton and tea to the ports for export. C-SST4.2 for the network, CG-SST2 for the colonial purpose the answer gives.
Cargo trains using 75-90 percent less energy than trucks. LO-123 for energy conservation, C-SST4.2 for the transport infrastructure being compared.
Vande Bharat trains running on electricity. C-SST4.2 for the service, LO-123 because the chapter's point is cleaner energy.
A mandi as the local hub where farmers bring and sell their crop. LO-137 is a genuine fit - the working of a local market - not the infrastructure fallback.
Morse's electric telegraph of 1844. Communications infrastructure history, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Coal, cement and cars as the heavy goods ships carry. Transport infrastructure, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Fibre cables, mobile towers, satellites and data centres as the elements of communication infrastructure. Competency-level C-SST4.2.
Connectivity bringing digital libraries and online classes to remote villages. C-SST4.2 for the infrastructure; the education benefit has no LO of its own in this frame.
E-governance explained through DigiLocker holding a driving licence. LO-138, a citizen's dealing with a government office, now online.
E-commerce as buying and selling over the internet. CG-SST4 for the market institution, LO-137 because it is the online counterpart of the local market that LO covers.
J.C. Bose demonstrating microwave transmission through walls in 1895. Communications technology, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Why Bose went unrecognised - he rarely patented his devices. Goal-level CG-SST4, matching the patent items, since the explanation turns on the institution of the patent.
A patent as the inventor's exclusive right to make, sell or use an invention. Goal-level CG-SST4 for an economic and legal institution.
Social infrastructure as schools, hospitals, libraries, fire stations and community centres. C-SST4.2 for local public provision, LO-138 because several are government offices in one's own locality.
Making infrastructure sustainable through eco-friendly materials, less harm to biodiversity and solar power. LO-123 for conservation of energy and flora, C-SST4.2 for the public works being built.
